Use case: precise-object-edit. Create a sprite-sheet COLORIZATION of image1, not a redesign. Image1 contains EXACTLY THREE existing Fire Emblem Gaiden swordsman idle sprites left-to-right. Image2 is OUR APPROVED MERCENARY and is the exclusive palette / flat pixel-art reference.
Preserve image1's ORIGINAL SWORDSMAN CLOTHING GEOMETRY AND POSES 1:1. The compact dark-haired head, short blue tunic, simple waist hem, short sleeves, exposed peach face/hands, dark legs and boots and especially the LARGE RECTANGULAR SHIELD are essential. Do not turn him into a detailed medieval armoured knight. The shield has a broad ivory rim and the original diagonal ivory stepped slash on a blue face; it is almost as tall as the entire upper body, top at head height, NOT a small shield at the hip. Preserve EXACT proportions, relative locations, native pixel silhouette, fixed head/body and fixed spread feet.
Idle pose0 (left): sword tip high at upper-left, inclined from left tip towards lower-right hand; large shield raised to crown height.
Idle pose1 (middle): tip stays at same height but shifts inward right, sword more upright; shield lowers ONE original pixel. Pose2 (right): tip shifts further right and blade becomes vertical; shield lowers ONE more pixel. Body/head/feet remain fixed.
COLOR ONLY using exactly these flat solid colors as in image2: dark navy #172638 (hair, outlines, boots, eyes), medium blue #3976B5 (tunic/shield), warm ivory #E4E1C8 (sleeves, trim, blade, shield border/motif), warm skin #DDA77D (face and hands). Clear dark pixel eye(s) remain visible on peach face, dark hair is one flat color. No white skin. No reflective armour, metallic highlights, gradients, brown hair, belts with buckles, ornamental shield diamond, added shoulder plates or extra costume details. Retain a crisp chunky pixel grid, no antialiasing. Same three cells horizontally, full bodies and complete swords/shields, transparent background, no captions, floor shadow only as in source. This is palette/material coloring of EXACT native outlines, not interpretation of their pose.
